questions.question: You are parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which direction should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels so your car rolls away from the center of the road if the brakes fail. Do this when parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.
Turn on your high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead of you better.
Keep your instrument panel lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can always stop within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: When can you legally turn left at a red traffic light after stopping?

options.text: When you are on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.
When you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
When you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: You may turn left at a red light only after you stop completely and you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street. Check for any signs that prohibit this turn.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, where should you look?

options.text: At the center of the roadway
At the right side of the road
Straight ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: At the right side of the road
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded. This lets you see enough of the road to stay on course. Do not use your bright lights to retaliate.

questions.question: You are in the left lane of a two-lane road. Many vehicles are passing you on the right. A driver behind you wants to drive faster. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane so you don't block traffic.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let other vehicles pass.
Move into the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to drive fast, pass, or turn left. Use the right lane when driving slower than other traffic, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Other vehicles that are also turning left
All approaching vehicles
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a "Walk" signal

questions.correctAnswerText: All approaching vehicles
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other vehicles that have a green light.

questions.question: Your tires feel like they lost contact with the road. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Ease off the gas and stay off the brakes. Wait for your tires to grip the road again before trying to stop or turn.

questions.question: Which of these roads is most likely to be slippery in cold, wet weather?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A residential road
A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze before the rest of the road and thaw out later. They are the most likely to be icy in cold, wet weather.

questions.question: How can you avoid hydroplaning while driving in rain?

options.text: Drive at the speed you would use in good weather.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose contact with the road and ride on top of the water. Driving more slowly in wet conditions is the best way to prevent this.

questions.question: A driver is passing you in a no passing zone. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Maintain your speed and position.
Slow down and let the other driver safely return to the driving lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the other driver safely return to the driving lane.
questions.explanation: Allow the passing vehicle to re-enter your lane easily. This helps everyone avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: Which statement is true about work zones on roads?

options.text: Fines for violations in work zones are the same as fines for regular traffic violations.
You must slow down for the cone zone.
Slow down only if you see workers present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down for the cone zone.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop for road equipment. Driving safely through work zones protects drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and road workers.

questions.question: If your vehicle's rear slides to the left, you should:

options.text: Not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left.
Turn your steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: If you skid on a wet or icy road, take your foot off the gas and do not use the brakes. Turn your wheel in the direction of the skid. If you have anti-lock brakes, press them firmly and steer straight.

questions.question: To make room for cars entering the freeway, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Move into a different lane.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into a different lane.
questions.explanation: Create space for vehicles entering the freeway. If possible, move to the next lane to let them in safely. If you cannot move lanes, adjust your speed to help them merge smoothly.

questions.question: When parallel parking, park within ____ of the curb.

options.text: Three feet
Two feet
One foot

questions.correctAnswerText: One foot
questions.explanation: Your wheels should be parallel to and one foot away from the curb. Only park where traffic can flow freely and drivers can see your vehicle from both directions.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:

options.text: Start to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Honk your horn loudly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn loudly.
questions.explanation: Use a loud horn blast if there is danger. Do this when a child or any pedestrian is about to step into the street in front of your moving vehicle.

questions.question: When a school bus picks up or drops off children, you must:

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction.
Slow down and get ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: When you see a school bus picking up or dropping off children, come to a complete stop before reaching the bus. You must stop regardless of which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you arrive at the same time as vehicles to your right and left, you should:

options.text: Let the vehicle on your left go first.
Let the vehicle on your right go first.
Wait until the intersection is clear before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When multiple vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Proceed in order of arrival after that.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are traveling the wrong way.
Treat the intersection as a stop sign.
Do not proceed until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
Merge to the right.
Turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that traffic may merge into your lane from the right.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.
Slow down and continue with caution.
Stop and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a full stop and proceed only when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Intersections ahead.
Road construction.
The road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to dangers ahead. This sign warns you about a curve to the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop and look both ways before going.
Let other traffic go first before you enter or cross.
Keep your speed and check for traffic from all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic go first before you enter or cross.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and be ready to stop if needed. Let any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian pass first. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: If your tire suddenly goes flat while driving:

options.text: Use the brakes gently.
Pump the brakes.
Press the brakes hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes gently.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Slow down by letting off the gas and using the brakes gently.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Change lanes in an intersection.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check for other drivers in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder. Watch for drivers trying to enter the same lane. Never change lanes or pass in an intersection.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should not:

options.text: Keep driving and find another route.
Drive to the next exit and turn around safely.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Do not back up in traffic or on the shoulder. Continue to the next exit or road. Other drivers do not expect a car backing toward them. Backing up will likely cause a crash.
